evidence.quote: Problem 19 (Stability of eventually positive semigroups). Let M be a von Neumann algebra equipped with a normal, semi-finite, and faithful trace τ and p ∈ [1, ∞). Let (etA )t∈[0,∞) be an individually eventually positive C0 - semigroup on Lp (M, τ ). Is s(A) = ω0 (A)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a von Neumann algebra equipped with a normal, semi-finite, faithful trace $\tau$, and let $p \in [1, \infty)$. Consider the associated noncommutative $L^p$-space $L^p(\mathcal{M}, \tau)$. Let $(e^{tA})_{t \geq 0}$ be a strongly continuous (i.e. $C_0$) semigroup on $L^p(\mathcal{M}, \tau)$ with generator $A$. Define the spectral bound $s(A) := \sup\{\operatorname{Re}\lambda : \lambda \in \sigma(A)\}$ and the exponential growth bound $\omega_0(A) := \inf\{w \in \mathbb{R} : \exists M \geq 1,\ \|e^{tA}\| \leq M e^{wt}\ \text{for all } t \geq 0\}$. Recall that the semigroup is called individually eventually positive if for every $x \in L^p(\mathcal{M}, \tau)$ with $x \geq 0$ there exists $t_0 = t_0(x) \geq 0$ such that $e^{tA} x \geq 0$ for all $t \geq t_0$, where positivity is taken with respect to the natural cone of positive elements in $L^p(\mathcal{M}, \tau)$.

Question: Under these assumptions, is it true that $s(A) = \omega_0(A)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about whether the classical Weis-type equality $s(A) = \omega_0(A)$, known for positive $C_0$-semigroups on (commutative) $L^p$-spaces, extends to individually eventually positive semigroups on noncommutative $L^p$-spaces. Recent surveys and works on eventually positive semigroups (spectral and asymptotic analysis) discuss related stability and spectral-bound questions but do not provide a resolution in the noncommutative $L^p$ setting. No published proof or counterexample was located.

status_evidence.title: Eventually positive semigroups: spectral and asymptotic analysis
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses spectral theory and stability of eventually positive semigroups; the equality s(A)=ω₀(A) on noncommutative L^p is not established.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys on eventually positive semigroups treat related spectral questions but do not resolve the noncommutative L^p case.

status_evidence.title: Stability criteria for positive semigroups on ordered Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Provides stability criteria via spectral and growth bounds for positive semigroups in ordered Banach space settings.
status_evidence.claim: Related stability results for positive semigroups exist but the eventually positive noncommutative L^p analogue is not settled.
